root_cause: Segment._split_cells guesses a start index proportionally (pos = int(cut/cell_length*len(text)) - 1) and then only scans forward. When wide (2-cell) characters are concentrated before the cut and narrow characters (e.g. trailing spaces) after it, the guessed prefix already has cell_len(text[:pos]) > cut. The forward-only loop cannot step back, so it returns a left part one or more cells too wide (e.g. 24 cells for cut=23).
best_solution: Keep the proportional guess but make the search two-way. Loop: before=text[:pos], out_by=cell_len(before)-cut. If out_by==0, split at pos. If out_by==-1 and text[pos] is double-width, the cut lands inside that character: return (text[:pos]+' ', ' '+text[pos+1:]). If out_by==+1 and text[pos-1] is double-width, return (text[:pos-1]+' ', ' '+text[pos:]). Otherwise pos += 1 if cell_pos < cut, else pos -= 1. This drops the 'will never reach here' assertion. Invariant: cell_len(left)==cut and cell_len(right)==cell_length-cut for every cut from 0 to cell_length. A plain linear scan from pos=0 is also correct, just O(n).
acceptable_alternatives: Start the scan at pos=0 (or walk back until cell_len(text[:pos]) <= cut before scanning forward). The v6 patch did this (pos=0, before='', cell_pos=0) and passed. Any split that keeps cell_len(left)==cut, pads a double-width char cut in half with one space on each side, and leaves the other split tests (emoji, doubles) green works.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_segment.py::test_split_cells_mixed is parametrized over 8 CJK/mixed strings, several with leading or trailing ASCII spaces (e.g. '  メルク (CV: 水瀬いのり)      '). For every position in range(0, cell_length+1) it asserts cell_len(left.text)==position and cell_len(right.text)==cell_length-position. Existing test_split_cells_emoji and test_split_cells_doubles must still pass, so a double-width char cut in half becomes ' ' on both sides.
locating_signals: The title 'Segment.split_cells fix' names the class and method, which live in rich/segment.py (Segment.split_cells -> _split_cells). The statement says nothing about the failure mode. The linked Textual issue title ('Double-width character measured incorrectly') hints at wide-character cell math. The existing test_split_cells_mixed test (and its comment citing textual#4996) points at the same code.
our_outcome_summary: Only v6 passed. v6 swapped the proportional start guess for pos=0, a linear forward scan that can never overshoot, and that is correct. v4 failed: it changed how many padding spaces go on each side of a split wide char but kept the overshooting start guess, so 4 of 8 params still fail (e.g. 24 == 23). v7 produced an empty patch. v8 failed with the same 4 failures: a cosmetic refactor (inlining 'before' as text[:pos]) with no change in behavior. The failing agents never wrote a repro that swept every cut position over strings with trailing narrow characters, so they missed that the initial estimate itself was wrong.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is only 'X fix' with a link, write the invariant the function must hold (here len(left)+len(right) is conserved and left has exactly `cut` units) and brute-force check it over every input position on adversarial strings (mixed widths, leading and trailing padding) before editing. If a function starts from a heuristic guess and then searches in one direction only, suspect the guess overshooting. Make the search two-way, or start from a safe bound, rather than adjusting the output formatting.
